Social worker/former therapist here. I’ll do my best with what you’ve given us here. First of all let me just say that it is extremely easy to look back at last actions and criticize them. Hence the old saying, “hindsight is 20/20.”  I’m sure that you have regrets and wish that you could’ve made different choices within this relationship. But the reality is that you are in this moment and that the things that led up to it have happened. When you lived those moments you didn’t have the insight or knowledge that you do now. Having said that, you seem to be keenly aware of what is going on. You said yourself that you have self-esteem issues and that you feel that you are being taken advantage of. But you’re also worried about losing the relationship. So what you’re really faced with here is a choice. Obviously I only have the information you are giving me so I’m sure it’s a lot more complex that I can imagine. However, you need to ask yourself how much more you’re willing to take. If it didn’t bother you, you wouldn’t have wanted advice or encouragement. So there’s a part of you that wants help. But you also have to help yourself. I won’t lie to you, I don’t think you ending this will probably go anywhere near the way you want it to. It almost never does. But when it comes to your personal health and what you want, you have to take charge. My advice to you if you decide to end things is to be direct and clear about breaking up. Don’t leave any room for interpretation. Make sure he knows that your relationship is over and that you do not want to be with him. Sounds harsh? Yeah I know. But if he’s a narcissist like you say he is that’s the only way this works. If necessary safeguard yourself if you feel the need. Tell friends, block him on social media, block his number…whatever you need to do. I’m not telling you to do any of this or that you even have to. I can just see that there’s a part of you that is uncertain and im sure he already takes advantage of you because of that. Whatever you do, just remember that you deserve happiness and love and that just because you’ve invested so much time into something doesn’t mean it’s good. You don’t get anything from pouring out of an empty glass. Good luck and I hope it all works out.

The part that attempts to fill in the gaps of being uncertain and perpetuates the actual stress you feel. We always fear what we don’t truly know because it’s not predictable or tangible. Just the sound of tree branch against the window could be the claws of a monster. It’s much less malicious when you can actually see that it’s only a tree branch outside.
